Subject: Thanks for the demo — few follow-ups on access and residency

Marcus,

Thanks for the demo today — team found the latency/cost examples helpful. Before we lock in next steps with procurement, our security group asked for a very focused set of confirmations around support access and data handling. High-level asks below — can you confirm by EOD Tuesday?

1) Break-glass / emergency support: who can access customer PII for live troubleshooting? What approvals are required and how is the access audited?
2) RBAC model: can you share a simple matrix showing roles that can read tokenized / raw inputs, and whether support engineers ever access raw payloads?
3) Logs & retention: sample log fields and default retention for request traces, KV cache traces, and audit records. We need evidence we can retain logs for 1 year and export to our SIEM.
4) Data residency: can we pin data processing to us-east-1 and ensure backups stay in-region? Any cross-region fallbacks?
5) PII: do you support redaction hooks or deterministic hashing at ingest? Is there a recommended pattern for not storing raw user inputs?

Attachments: I attached the template our security ops team uses (simple checklist) — happy to map answers into it.

Olivia
Head of Security Operations
FinTrust

Hi Olivia — great meeting, and thanks for laying out the asks so clearly. I captured short answers below and attached a compact support-access pack we use for security reviews. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min tech deep-dive with our security engineering team (Soojin) and Solutions (Ben) to walk through controls and sample logs.

Answers (short):
1) Break-glass: Redwood enforces a tiered access model. Production break-glass requires a two-person approval (on-call lead + security approver) and is recorded in an immutably timestamped audit log with session video metadata when elevated terminal access occurs. All elevated sessions generate an approval ticket and are forwarded to customer-designated auditors on request.

2) RBAC: Role-based model is declarative. Default roles: Viewer, Operator, Support-Read, Support-Session, Admin. Support-Read can see metadata and aggregated metrics only; Support-Session allows ephemeral access to sanitized request payloads with explicit justification recorded. We do not grant default support engineers persistent access to raw PII; persistent raw access is restricted to Admins with documented business justification. I'll attach the RBAC matrix.

3) Logs & retention: Default: request metadata and token-level billing logs retained 90 days; full request traces and debug artifacts retained 30 days by default. For enterprise customers (Dedicated/Private) we support custom retention policies up to 12 months and exports to S3 / SIEM connectors. Log samples attached.

4) Data residency: Hosted processing is region-pinned; for FinTrust we can pin to us-east-1. Backups and snapshots can be restricted to in-region options; cross-region failover is opt-in and would require contractual agreement.

5) PII handling: We support pre-ingest deterministic hashing and configurable redaction hooks via the ingestion pipeline. We also provide built-in masking transforms that can remove or replace PII before it's written to persistent traces. Recommended pattern: use client-side hashing for highest assurance + server-side masking for defense-in-depth.

Next steps suggested:
- I'll send our brief Support Access pack (attached) and RBAC matrix.
- If FinTrust wants retention >90 days, I'll open an internal ticket for a custom retention profile and pricing.
- Proposed tech Q/A with Soojin and Ben — do you prefer Tue 2pm or Wed 11am ET?

Attachments: redwood_support-access-overview.pdf, redwood_rbac-matrix.csv, redwood_audit-log-sample.txt

Cheers,
Marcus Lin

Marcus / Ben / Olivia — attaching the short pack and inline answers. Kept it tight for FinTrust security ops.

Summary (inline):
- Break-glass: event flows through our ticketing + approval service. Emergency session requires approval from on-call lead AND a named Redwood security approver; the session is time-boxed, recorded at the network level, and a session digest is written into the immutable audit log (timestamp, approver IDs, justification). Samples: redwood_audit-log-sample.txt.

- RBAC: See attached matrix (redwood_rbac-matrix.csv). TL;DR: Support-Read = metrics & aggregated metadata; Support-Session = ephemeral, masked payloads by default; Admin = able to request raw payloads with explicit ticket + two-person approval. Default support engineers do NOT have raw persistent access.

- Logs & retention: For Hosted accounts we can configure exports to your S3 bucket or push to Splunk/Datadog. Standard limits exist in hosted; we can enable 12-month retention under an enterprise retention profile (requires committed contract). Attached: redwood_audit-log-sample.txt (truncated) and a short slide with export options.

- Data residency: Confirmed — we can pin processing to us-east-1. Backups can be configured to remain in-region; cross-region failover is disabled unless contractually authorized.

- PII controls: Support pre-ingest client hashing; server-side masking; ingestion hooks that call a customer-supplied redaction function (in Private deployments). Guidance: client hashing + server masking + limited retention is the pattern our bigger finance customers use.

Attachments included: redwood_support-access-overview.pdf, redwood_rbac-matrix.csv, redwood_audit-log-sample.txt

If this looks good, Marcus — I recommend we offer Tue 2pm ET for the deeper session (Soojin + Ben + product security). Olivia — does that work?
